raw_signal: יש רק CTA אחד, אבל העין שלי הולכת קודם לכפתור המשני.

candidate_mechanisms.name: visual salience mismatch
candidate_mechanisms.explains: The interface visually ranks a secondary action above the owner's intended next action.
candidate_mechanisms.does_not_explain: It does not establish that external users fail to find the intended action.
candidate_mechanisms.discriminator: Normalize fill and placement while preserving the actions and compare which element becomes perceptually primary.

evidence.description: In the integrated screen, the secondary control is filled and positioned above the intended outlined primary action.
External design/perception evidence supports treating fill, placement and visual rank as salience mechanisms without equating salience with task success.
During real use, the owner reports that their eye goes to the secondary control first and confirms the intended product priority is the other action.
The current visual state can be rendered in the deployed product, but no third-party perception has yet been observed.

claims.statement: The secondary control has stronger visual salience cues than the intended primary action in the integrated screen.
Fill and placement are plausible mechanisms for the observed salience mismatch; this mechanism does not imply external task failure.
A reversible rebalance of fill and placement is justified while preserving the action set and state transition.
External users will identify the intended action first after the salience rebalance.

design_distinction: Visual salience can conflict with product-state priority without yet establishing external task failure.
intervention: Rebalance fill and placement so the owner's intended primary action is visually dominant, without changing the number of actions or the state transition.
must_not_change: Do not change the action set, navigation or underlying transition while testing the salience intervention.
perceptual_success_criterion: For the owner in the same real-use state, the intended action becomes the first actionable element their eye ranks; external-user discovery remains a separate field claim.

gate.falsifier: If normalizing fill and placement does not change the owner's perceptual ranking, salience mismatch is insufficient to explain the signal.
gate.positive_control: Create a deliberate reverse-salience variant in which the secondary action is even more visually dominant; the comparison must detect the ranking change rather than remaining green regardless of styling.

reversal_condition: If the intended action is already perceptually primary after controlling fill and placement, or if the complaint persists unchanged, reopen neighboring mechanisms instead of escalating the same diagnosis.
field_requirement: If the product decision depends on stranger task discovery, observe external users entering this state without prompting and record which actionable element they identify or choose first.
next_step: Implement the reversible salience variant and run the specified owner/repo discriminator; do not claim external-user improvement yet.
